gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-fs-pilcrow-rounded: Wide-set and unmistakably techy, Bruno Ace SC strings its letters out like beads on a thread. Pilcrow Rounded tucks its sans-serif letters in tight, with big open counters; shrink the heading and that spacing contrast gets lost.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-fs-quicksand: Distinctive from the first glance, Bruno Ace SC spaces its letters wide and never thins a stroke. And Quicksand, a plain sans of blown-glass bowls and rounded terminals, keeps a long page of text light and friendly.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-alan-sans: Alan Sans keeps the curve tails pulled back from its letters, a restrained body that stays out of the way. And Bruno Ace SC, drawn like a technical pen line, does its best work at the top, where its wide letters can show off.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-albert-sans: Contemporary in feel, Bruno Ace SC spreads its open-mouthed letters wide and never thins a stroke, while Albert Sans holds steady below. Its apertures stay open even at tiny sizes.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-alef: Drawn with the line weight of a technical pen, Bruno Ace SC sits wide on the page beside Alef, whose open-ended curves keep things modern. The sharpest thing here is that mechanical-versus-plain tension.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-alegreya-sans-sc: Wide, hairline-free and a bit futuristic, Bruno Ace SC leads without a single swell. And Alegreya Sans SC, a plain sans with a welcoming gap in the c, follows it down the page in a lower, quieter key.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-almarai: Beaded, wide and technical, Bruno Ace SC draws every letter with open apertures and no calligraphic thinning. And Almarai, a sans-serif whose line never swells or tapers, fills the text beneath it without pinching a letter shut.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-amarna: Wide letters on a long thread: that is Bruno Ace SC, expressive and free of any thinning stroke. But Amarna, a sans with contrast-free strokes and unclogged small counters, does the quiet work beneath it.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-andika: Spaced-out and bold in personality, Bruno Ace SC keeps its apertures open and its strokes untapered. And Andika, a sans-serif with wide, easy s shapes, wants its size nudged up so those thick tails can breathe.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-anta: Open apertures and no calligraphic thinning give Bruno Ace SC its beads-on-a-thread look, wide and expressive. Anta, a sans bent like wire with gaping e mouths, should be sized up a notch so that shape reads.
